name: Discord
verdict: Self-serve: create an application and use OAuth plus a bot, with no review. Verification is required as the app grows toward 100 servers and privileged intents need approval; customers need Manage Server to add the bot.
needGuide: Short one, but plan for verification and privileged-intent approval if you expect to pass about 100 servers.

auth.detail: Authorization-code grant with refresh tokens (PKCE recommended), plus a bot authorization flow (scope=bot, no redirect) that adds a bot token user to a guild. Access token expires_in example is 604800 s (7 days). Redirect URIs must be registered. Revoking any token revokes the whole authorization.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review) | days to weeks if verification and intents approval are needed

approval.gate: Verification is required as an app grows toward 100 servers (Discord's help center warns from 75; the API docs I fetched say 100 or more). Privileged intents (GUILD_PRESENCES, GUILD_MEMBERS, MESSAGE_CONTENT) must be approved for verified-eligible apps. Some scopes (dm_channels.read, voice, rpc.*, relationships.read) are partner-only.
approval.atScale: Verification once the bot nears 100 servers; privileged intents need approval

scopes.why: Common scopes are self-serve, but dm_channels.read, voice and rpc.* are approval-only and the message content intent is privileged.
scopes.summary: Common: identify, email, guilds, guilds.members.read, connections, bot, applications.commands, webhook.incoming. Approval-only: dm_channels.read, identify.premium, voice, rpc.*, relationships.read (Social SDK). Message content intent is privileged.

prerequisites: Account and owner: Any Discord account can create the app; use a Team (company-owned) rather than a personal account so ownership survives staff changes.
Where you register: Developer Portal → New Application → OAuth2 → add Redirects, copy Client ID/Secret; Bot page → Reset Token and set Privileged Gateway Intents

registerAt.path: Developer Portal → New Application → OAuth2 → add Redirects, copy Client ID/Secret; Bot page → Reset Token and set Privileged Gateway Intents

steps.do: Create a Team and a New Application at discord.com/developers/applications
OAuth2 page: add HTTPS redirect URIs; copy Client ID and Secret
Implement authorization code + PKCE and refresh-token handling; check the iss parameter
If a bot is needed, build the invite URL with scope=bot applications.commands and minimal permissions
Enable only needed Privileged Gateway Intents on the Bot page
Test in a dev server; watch guild count and Developer Portal notices
Before reaching the cap, start App Verification and privileged-intent applications with use-case write-ups

roles.team: Any Discord account can create the app; use a Team (company-owned) rather than a personal account so ownership survives staff changes.
roles.console: Developer Portal Teams: create a team and invite members by username (likely; not verified), then transfer the app to the team.
roles.customer: To add the bot to a server the user needs Manage Server permission in that guild. For user OAuth (identify, guilds) any user can authorize.

testing: Use your own test server; bots in fewer than 100 servers can use limited privileged-intent toggles in the Bot page.
Apps under about 10,000 unique users can enable privileged intents without review per the gateway doc.

blockers.problem: Bot growth hits the verification threshold
blockers.fix: Apply early; pending verification can block adding servers (VERIFICATION_PENDING_GUILD_LIMIT flag).

blockers.problem: Gateway closes with 4014 if you request an intent not enabled or approved
Self-botting or automating user accounts is prohibited
Team apps limited to identify and applications.commands.update for client credentials

automation.agentCan: Write OAuth and bot code, configure slash commands via API, draft verification and intent justifications, run test calls.
automation.humanMust: Portal login, team setup, owner identity verification and verification submission (likely third-party ID check), accepting Developer Policy.

uncertain: Could not load Discord's verification help-center articles (fetch errors, then quota exhausted), so the 75-server notice, 100-server cap, ID-verification method and review timeline are unconfirmed; the API docs conflict on thresholds (100+ servers vs 10,000 users).
